title: The known 1.13-cycle-per-day doublet of KIC 5520878 recurs in Kepler quarters 11 to 17
abstract: We test whether two known weak signals of KIC 5520878 persist beyond the early Kepler data used to identify them. In release 25 raw aperture flux, their fixed-frequency amplitudes in quarters 11 to 17 are 0.410 and 0.332 millimagnitudes. Both recur in quarters 11 to 13 and quarters 14 to 17. The higher sum-frequency component also recurs. The lower sum-frequency component is less stable under nearby-frequency and window-sign controls. Raw-flux results change little across 10-, 20-, and 30-day nuisance fits. Corrected flux retains the low-frequency pair but has more nearby spectral structure. Flux-unit fits reduce reliance on the magnitude transform. Conditional errors omit long correlations and signal-model error. These observations support persistence of the known doublet, but do not identify a stellar mode or exclude detector effects and blends. No new object or independent telescope confirmation is claimed. Code, selected observations, exact input hashes, tables, controls, and retrieval instructions are included.
